--- a/minbpe/_rare.py
+++ b/minbpe/_rare.py
@@ -0,0 +1,108 @@
+"""
+Code paths that most programs never run (long-sequence encoding, saving).
+Kept out of the package import so that importing minbpe stays cheap; the
+callers in base.py import this module on first use.
+"""
+from heapq import heapify, heappop, heappush
+
+
+def apply_merges_heap(ids, merges):
+    """
+    Same result as base.apply_merges, for long sequences: a doubly linked list
+    over the original positions plus a heap of (rank, position) entries for
+    every mergeable adjacent pair. Entries are validated lazily when popped (a
+    pair whose tokens changed is recomputed), and each round pops all entries
+    of the minimal rank in position order. The first valid one picks the pair
+    (same as the first-seen minimal pair); its occurrences are merged left to
+    right, skipping overlaps, exactly like merge().
+    """
+    merges_get = merges.get
+    n = len(ids)
+    val = list(ids)
+    nxt = list(range(1, n + 1)) # n means "no next"
+    prv = list(range(-1, n - 1)) # -1 means "no previous"
+    heap = [(r, i) for i, r in enumerate(map(merges_get, zip(val, val[1:])))
+            if r is not None]
+    heapify(heap)
+    while heap:
+        r = heap[0][0]
+        pair = None
+        last = -1
+        merged = []
+        rest = []
+        while heap and heap[0][0] == r:
+            p = heappop(heap)[1]
+            if p == last:
+                continue # duplicate entry (pops come out in position order)
+            last = p
+            v = val[p]
+            if v is None:
+                continue # position was merged away
+            q = nxt[p]
+            if q == n:
+                continue
+            pr = (v, val[q])
+            if merges_get(pr) != r:
+                continue # stale entry
+            if pair is None:
+                pair = pr
+            elif pr != pair:
+                rest.append(p) # another pair with the same rank: later round
+                continue
+            val[p] = r
+            val[q] = None
+            q2 = nxt[q]
+            nxt[p] = q2
+            if q2 < n:
+                prv[q2] = p
+            merged.append(p)
+        for p in rest:
+            heappush(heap, (r, p))
+        for p in merged:
+            a = prv[p]
+            if a >= 0:
+                rk = merges_get((val[a], r))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, a))
+            b = nxt[p]
+            if b < n:
+                rk = merges_get((r, val[b]))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, p))
+    return [v for v in val if v is not None]
+
+
+def save(tok, file_prefix):
+    """Implementation of Tokenizer.save (see there)."""
+    from .base import render_token
+    # write the model: to be used in load() later
+    model_file = file_prefix + ".model"
+    with open(model_file, 'w') as f:
+        # write the version, pattern and merges, that's all that's needed
+        f.write("minbpe v1\n")
+        f.write(f"{tok.pattern}\n")
+        # write the special tokens, first the number of them, then each one
+        f.write(f"{len(tok.special_tokens)}\n")
+        for special, idx in tok.special_tokens.items():
+            f.write(f"{special} {idx}\n")
+        # the merges dict
+        for idx1, idx2 in tok.merges:
+            f.write(f"{idx1} {idx2}\n")
+    # write the vocab: for the human to look at (tokens may be partial utf-8
+    # sequences, rendered lossily with errors='replace', so load() can't use it)
+    vocab_file = file_prefix + ".vocab"
+    inverted_merges = {idx: pair for pair, idx in tok.merges.items()}
+    with open(vocab_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        for idx, token in tok.vocab.items():
+            s = render_token(token)
+            # find the children of this token, if any
+            if idx in inverted_merges:
+                # if this token has children, render it nicely as a merge
+                idx0, idx1 = inverted_merges[idx]
+                s0 = render_token(tok.vocab[idx0])
+                s1 = render_token(tok.vocab[idx1])
+                f.write(f"[{s0}][{s1}] -> [{s}] {idx}\n")
+            else:
+                # otherwise this is leaf token, just print it
+                f.write(f"[{s}] {idx}\n")
+
